eyebrow: A plain split can get unlucky
code:
_, _, _, y_te = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2)
_, _, _, y_te_s = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y)
print(round(y_te.mean(),3))     # 0.13 -- plain: drifted from 0.09!
print(round(y_te_s.mean(),3))   # 0.09 -- stratified: exact match
caption: stratify=y forces every split to keep the same class proportions.
Real output: plain split std = 0.0253 (wanders). Stratified std = 0.0 (pinned to the truth).

eyebrow: A three-way split: call it twice
code:
X_temp, X_test, y_temp, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.20, stratify=y)
X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(X_temp, y_temp, test_size=0.25, stratify=y_temp)
print(len(X_train), len(X_val), len(X_test))   # 300 100 100
caption: 0.25 of the remaining 80% = 20% of the total -- a clean 60/20/20.
